summary: The school technology leader argues against the termination of E-Rate, emphasizing the ongoing need for the program to support network infrastructure, cybersecurity, and other educational technologies. The funding has been crucial in maintaining reliable connectivity and infrastructure across the organization's campuses, which would otherwise require local absorption of costs and potential redirection of funds from other educational priorities. The FCC should allow the Cybersecurity Pilot Program to complete its work and use the resulting data to evaluate the cybersecurity needs of schools and libraries. The pilot provides an opportunity to determine the actual costs and operational experience of cybersecurity needs. The program should be allowed to evolve with those needs, with continued investment in Category One and Category Two services and careful consideration of the findings of the Cybersecurity Pilot Program.
